title: SHIFT(hold) + NUMBER not working to switch between Fancy zones personal layouts

judgment.rationale: Current code and recent test history identify the exact modifier gate behind the regression, but product intent for restoring the legacy shortcut must be confirmed.
evidence: Multiple users reproduce loss of Shift+number in 0.101.2362.
Recent history added active-drag quick-layout coverage and Shift-state hardening.
Reporter separated older placement issues from this regression.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm shortcut ownership, then approve a guarded compatibility design.

fix_assessment.rationale: No open or merged fix attempt was found for issue #50149.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones quick layout switching by Shift+number while dragging regressed in 0.101.2362. Current code explicitly requires Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit during dragging, while users describe the prior Shift+number/non-primary-button flow.
known_information: Issue is open and labeled Product-FancyZones.
Reporter and commenters reproduce the regression in 0.101.2362.
Current FancyZones.cpp requires Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit while dragging.
Recent commit d68980a added active-drag quick-layout tests and fixed swallowed Shift state.
Two other placement reports were explicitly separated by the reporter.
inferences: The new modifier requirement likely replaced or bypassed the former interaction.
Restoration must avoid reintroducing the old 'steals number keys' bug.
issue_context.analysis: The regression is reproducible and the branch contains the exact gating logic. The design should restore compatibility only with robust drag-state and key-consumption rules.
initial_investigation: Read d68980a history and its active-drag tests.

information_gaps.information: Whether Shift+number remains the supported product shortcut
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines compatibility fix versus intentional new behavior
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm current shortcut contract and test both configured mouse-button modes

proposed_fixes.title: Restore safe Shift+number quick-layout switching during drag
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Current code accepts only Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit while dragging, so the prior Shift+number path is not dispatched.
plan: Add a guarded Shift+digit path only for a valid active drag and configured layout.
Update drag/Shift state before swallowing input.
Extend UI tests for primary/non-primary activation and stuck-drag recovery.
verification: Drag a window and switch with Shift+1/2.
Verify bare Shift+number outside valid drag reaches the foreground app.

confidence.rationale: The gating logic and regression are clear, but product intent for the legacy shortcut needs confirmation.

design.root_cause: FancyZones requires Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit while dragging; Shift+digit is not accepted by OnKeyDown.
evidence: FancyZones.cpp lines 715-743 require Win+Ctrl+Alt while dragging.
Multiple users reproduce loss of Shift+number.
Recent commit d68980a hardened active-drag Shift state.

symbols: quick-layout switching during active window drag

affected_files.purpose: Drag validity used to guard keyboard ownership

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Only Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit is accepted during dragging.
implementation_steps.change: Add documented, guarded Shift+digit compatibility only for a real drag and configured layout while preserving explicit-chord behavior.
implementation_steps.code_block: bool legacyQuickLayout = dragging && shift && digitPressed != -1 && IsValidDragSession(); if (legacyQuickLayout || explicitChord) PostMessageW(m_window, WM_PRIV_QUICK_LAYOUT_KEY, 0, digitPressed);
edge_cases: Do not swallow outside valid drag

verify: Build FancyZones and focused UI tests.
risks: Low-level keyboard ownership can affect typing during drag.
Legacy behavior may conflict with newer documented shortcut.
alternatives: Keep only Win+Ctrl+Alt; rejected because it regresses established workflow.
Change documentation only; rejected because code does not accept Shift+digit.

comment.body: Current FancyZones accepts Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit while dragging, while the report and multiple follow-ups confirm Shift+number worked before 0.101.2362. Please confirm whether Shift+number remains supported for both primary and non-primary mouse activation. This determines whether to restore compatibility or document the newer chord as intentional.
